observation.visible_scene: A golf-ball dispensing/sorting rig: a white tray holds a loose cluster of dimpled balls in teal, silver, green, yellow, red, blue and magenta, while a rail on the right carries black clamp fixtures gripping dark balls. In the foreground a large curved transparent (glass-like) panel scoops around the tray, and a big polished metallic cylinder sits at the upper right; wood flooring is visible at the left. Three balls (magenta, silver, black) rest on the curved transparent panel, and colored reflections of the tray balls appear on its surface.
visible_changes: The dominant change is camera motion: a continuous zoom-in combined with an orbital/pan move toward the curved transparent panel. As the camera advances, the tray of multicolored balls and the upper-right metallic cylinder slide out of the top of the frame, while a white conical/funnel shape enters on the right.

The cluster of colored balls on the white tray stays mutually static (no repositioning relative to one another) throughout the excerpt; their apparent drift is due to camera movement, not object motion.

On the curved transparent panel the magenta, silver and black balls shift in apparent position relative to each other and to the panel (the black ball moves toward/below the silver one), an effect consistent with the rotating viewpoint and possibly a slow roll along the curve.

Reflections on the transparent panel (e.g., the purple blob at left, the cyan blob at lower-left, the magenta streak) change shape and location as the viewing angle changes; these are reflections, not separate objects.
The black clamp fixtures on the right rail remain fixed relative to the tray and exit the frame as the camera zooms in.
outside_clip_unknowns: Whether the balls on the curved panel roll off or remain, and what happens to the tray balls after the excerpt ends.
The cause of the camera move and the full layout/function of the machine beyond the cropped view.
Any earlier or later contact/launch events not shown.
uncertain_details: Cannot fully separate true rolling of the magenta/silver/black balls on the panel from apparent motion caused by the camera orbit.
The exact camera trajectory (pure zoom vs. zoom-plus-rotation) and the material identity of the curved transparent surface are inferred from reflections only.
The static interval of the tray balls is relative to each other; absolute scene motion cannot be confirmed.
